issue: The comment "Keep every projection row as a candidate; unseeded rows receive no cosine match" is false, and the behavior it describes is what the ablation now measures. createFixtureProjection sets source:"fixture" (projection.ts:1882), so scoreSemanticShadowLane builds fixtureVectors for every projection row (semantic-shadow.ts:352-357) and falls back to it at semantic-shadow.ts:394. Unseeded rows therefore do get a cosine match: a 32-dim hash vector (semantic-shadow.ts:103) compared against the real 768-dim prompt vector, which cosineSimilarity truncates to Math.min(left.length, right.length) = 32 (semantic-shadow.ts:78). The projection carries 63 command rows while readCommandEmbeddingSources() returns 47 TypeScript-enabled sources, so 16 command rows are unseeded and scored on that truncated comparison. The pollution biases the full arm toward more matches, which is the direction that would wrongly promote the lane to a live weight, and this test is the gate that decides DEFAULT_SCORER_LANE_WEIGHTS.semantic_shadow. The current verdict is unaffected (default stays 0), so this is latent rather than active.

issue: The root README's Skill Routing section describes the advisor as a resident daemon and says nothing about the capability this scope adds: after startup IPC is ready and after each watcher reindex the daemon now checks skill and command vector coverage and, when coverage is incomplete, probes Ollama once and embeds missing or stale rows. That is a new background network call to Ollama on daemon start, and it is the headline of the skill's v1.3.0.0 changelog. The root README is the only place a reader learns what the advisor does at this level, and neither README.md:203 nor the standalone-skill line at README.md:299 reflects it. The skill README, INSTALL-GUIDE and feature catalog all describe it, so the gap is the root README alone.

The skill README tells a reader to set SPECKIT_ADVISOR_LANE_WEIGHTS_JSON='{"semantic_shadow":0.05}' 'to enable its live scoring' and stops there. The scope adds a precondition the same release note states at .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.1.0.0.md:227: raising the weight requires current vectors for every embeddable skill and command. semantic-shadow.ts:383-385 returns an empty match list with disabledReason 'incomplete_skill_vectors' when any required row lacks a vector, so a reader who follows the README right after upgrading gets no semantic scoring and no explanation. The README's next sentence, that the background refresh runs at any lane weight, does not state the precondition.

The open release note now contradicts itself about whether the daemon probes a backend. Line 220, unchanged by this scope, says the embedder 'points straight to its one registered model at daemon start, with no backend probes'. The scope adds line 226 in the next section: 'Incomplete coverage triggers one Ollama probe'. Both statements sit in the same Skill Advisor block of the same release note, so a reader cannot tell whether the daemon contacts Ollama. The scope added the probe and did not qualify the older sentence, which is now true only of pointer resolution.
